title: Dynamic Compression in Recurrent Networks
abstract: arXiv:2608.17896v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Recurrent models process long contexts efficiently by compressing their history into a fixed-size state, but modern architectures typically do so in a single causal pass over the sequence. Each input must therefore be compressed before the model knows how it will later be used, forcing a limited state to compromise across possible future demands. We introduce dynamic compression, which allows a recurrent model to selectively revisit past tokens and revise its fixed-size state through additional recurrent updates. The model need not preserve every part of the history at uniformly high fidelity in its recurrent state, because lower-fidelity information can be revisited from the retained raw sequence when it becomes relevant. translated_title: 递归网络中的动态压缩
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.17896v1 公告类型：新论文 摘要：递归模型通过将长上下文压缩为固定大小的状态来高效处理长序列，但现代架构通常以单次因果遍历序列的方式实现这一点。因此，每个输入必须在模型知道其后续用途之前被压缩，这迫使有限的状态在潜在的未来需求之间做出妥协。我们引入了动态压缩，它允许递归模型有选择性地重新访问过去的标记，并通过额外的递归更新来修正其固定大小的状态。模型无需在其递归状态中以均匀高保真度保存历史的每个部分，因为当较低保真度的信息变得相关时，可以从保留的原始序列中重新访问。我们在一个受控环境中研究这一点，其中模型首先在上下文中学习多个函数，然后在同一序列的后续部分遇到一系列少样本任务，每个任务要求其识别并重用其中一个函数。
tldr: 本文提出动态压缩机制，允许递归模型在序列处理中通过选择性重访过去标记并更新固定状态，从而在无需高保真存储全部历史的情况下高效适应后续任务需求。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces dynamic compression, enabling recurrent models to selectively revisit past tokens and revise their fixed-size state, thereby efficiently adapting to later task demands without storing the entire history at high fidelity.
